prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near foreground tool and the camera wearer’s hands, roughly 0.2–0.7 m away, from the bench and red rails at about 0.7–2 m and the people and equipment farther ahead at roughly 3–7 m. It shows the tool remaining within arm’s reach while shifting from lower centre-left toward the lower-right region as the wearer turns, with the background sliding laterally but not clearly approaching or retreating. Nearby foreground objects occlude parts of the bench and floor, while distant people are partly occluded by machinery and shelving; some objects also extend beyond the bottom and side edges. This relative depth ordering is clearer than in RGB, but exact metre estimates, distant-person boundaries, thin structures, and dark upper-background regions appear unreliable or smoothed together.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several distant people across the five frames, generally clustered in front of the wearer at about 3–7 m and separated from one another by roughly 0.5–3 m, while also marking a chair, suitcase-like object, and a supposed cell phone. Most detected people occupy the upper or middle background, whereas a large near mask at the lower left corresponds to the camera wearer’s visible hand/arm and tool area within about 0.2–0.7 m; this foreground region partly occludes the bench. Across frames, the distant masks move left or right mainly with the wearer’s turning, and no strong approach or retreat is evident; facing direction and direct gaze cannot be established reliably from these masks. The map makes small, partially occluded people easier to locate than RGB, but it misses much of the furniture and machinery, fragments some people, inconsistently detects the foreground arm, and likely mislabels parts of the held tool as a person or cell phone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a magenta hand skeleton in the first two frames, located low and left of centre at approximately 0.3–0.6 m, confirming that the wearer’s hand is close, below the main scene, and extended around the foreground tool. The hand shifts rightward and changes projected orientation between those frames, consistent with relative hand or camera rotation, then disappears entirely in frames three through five despite the hand/tool remaining visible in RGB. No body skeletons are recovered for the people roughly 3–7 m ahead, so their mutual spacing, facing direction, gaze, reach, and partial occlusions cannot be inferred from this map. It reveals finger and wrist geometry that is difficult to resolve in RGB, but its severe missed detections and lack of depth make it unreliable beyond the two near-hand observations.
